note: A fictional multi-tenant SaaS backend. Decisions span unrelated subsystems on purpose, so should_miss probes can prove a decision stays out of an area it does not govern (the relevance-scoping claim). The last two decisions are a reversal pair for the evolution check.

decisions.content: Decision: auth uses server-side opaque session tokens, not JWTs.
decisions.source_text: Why: we need instant revocation on logout and breach response. A JWT cannot be revoked before expiry without a denylist that defeats its statelessness. Rejected: stateless JWTs. Chose opaque tokens backed by a sessions table.

decisions.content: Decision: monetary amounts are stored as integer minor units (cents), never floats.
decisions.source_text: Why: float arithmetic introduces rounding drift that corrupts ledgers over time. Rejected: Decimal columns, which still risk app-layer float coercion. Chose integer cents alongside a currency-code column.

decisions.content: Decision: every payment-mutating endpoint requires a client idempotency key.
decisions.source_text: Why: provider webhooks and client retries double-charge without it. Rejected: a dedupe heuristic on (user, amount, minute), which is fragile. Chose mandatory idempotency keys persisted with the charge.

decisions.content: Decision: search queries hit a denormalized read model, never the OLTP tables directly.
decisions.source_text: Why: full-text scans on transactional tables lock rows and degrade writes. Rejected: querying live tables with GIN indexes. Chose a projected search document rebuilt from change events.

decisions.content: Decision: uploads are content-addressed by sha256; client filenames are never trusted for storage paths.
decisions.source_text: Why: trusting filenames enables path traversal and collisions. Rejected: sanitizing user filenames. Chose hashing content to derive the storage key, keeping the original name only as display metadata.

decisions.content: Decision: the API returns errors in a typed envelope {code, message, details}, never raw exceptions.
decisions.source_text: Why: leaking stack traces is a security and DX problem, and clients need stable machine-readable codes. Rejected: HTTP status alone. Chose a typed error envelope with a documented code registry.

decisions.content: Decision: tenant isolation is enforced in the database with row-level security, not application-layer filters.
decisions.source_text: Why: a forgotten tenant_id clause leaks data across tenants; app-layer enforcement is one bug from a breach. Rejected: a shared base-query helper. Chose Postgres RLS policies keyed on a per-session tenant setting.

decisions.content: Decision: configuration comes only from environment variables validated at boot; no config files in the image.
decisions.source_text: Why: baking config into images causes drift between environments and leaks secrets into the registry. Rejected: per-environment TOML files. Chose env vars with a fail-fast schema check on startup.

decisions.content: Decision: database migrations are forward-only; there are no down-migrations in production.
decisions.source_text: Why: down-migrations are rarely tested and dangerous under load; rollbacks happen by deploying a new forward migration. Rejected: reversible up/down pairs. Chose forward-only with expand-contract for breaking changes.

decisions.content: Decision: API versioning lives in the URL path (/v1/), not in a header.
decisions.source_text: Why: path versions are cacheable, visible in logs, and trivial to route; header versioning hides the contract. Rejected: Accept-header content negotiation. Chose /vN/ path prefixes.

decisions.content: Decision: background jobs are dispatched via Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY.
decisions.source_text: Why: avoids running a separate broker since we already run Postgres. Trade-off accepted: no persistence of notifications missed while no worker is listening.

decisions.content: Decision: background jobs use a durable jobs table polled with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
decisions.source_text: Why: LISTEN/NOTIFY silently dropped jobs whenever no worker was connected (deploys, crashes), with no recovery. This reverses the earlier LISTEN/NOTIFY choice. Chose a persisted jobs table so missed work is retried, with SKIP LOCKED for safe concurrent workers.
